title: When the Colony Falls Again
premise: Paloma Sterling, the last human technician aboard relay station Vesper-9, has spent six years recording the quiet erasure of the colony it once served — a world whose transmissions stopped, whose records were rewritten, and whose name no one in the Core answers about. When the deep-space ship Meridian returns carrying colonists who have aged backward into childhood, Paloma becomes the only living witness who remembers what actually happened: a massacre ordered to protect an inheritance of terraforming patents. As the children's memories surface and the station's corrupted archives begin fighting back, Paloma must smuggle the truth out before the same corporate fleet that erased the colony arrives to erase him. The story ends with Paloma broadcasting the unaltered record on every channel, dying as the signal goes out, while the children — the colony's true heirs — carry the memory home.
about_author: Sable Almeida is a former radio archivist from the Azores who spent a decade restoring damaged oral-history recordings before turning to fiction. Their work explores how institutions rewrite the past and how ordinary people keep honest records anyway.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Establishes daily life on automated relay station Vesper-9: maintenance rituals, one-way messages to a silent colony, and his private audio log of 'things that used to be.' Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into stubborn devotion.

chapters.title: What the Archive Forgets
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. He discovers a file he recorded years ago has been altered — a colony transmission replaced with static and a falsified quarantine notice. Emotional beat: first cold dread that someone is still watching the station.

chapters.title: A Light That Shouldn't Return
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The ship Meridian appears on long-range sensors, broadcasting a colony registry code retired seven years ago. He prepares docking protocols for ghosts. Emotional beat: hope curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: POV alternating Paloma and Ilsa, a woman now physically eight years old. The survivors disembark: forty-one colonists aged backward, memories fragmented, bodies wrong. Emotional beat: uncanny tenderness and horror.

chapters.title: Ilsa Remembers Rain
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. She recalls her daughter, her garden, her death — sensory flashes of fire and sealed doors. She doesn't understand why she is small again. Emotional beat: grief without context.

chapters.title: The Meridian's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The ship's crew complement reads zero; its logs end mid-sentence at the moment of return. Something or someone brought them back, but not kindly. Emotional beat: mounting suspicion.

chapters.title: Patents and Ash
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Digging through pre-collapse records, he finds the motive: the Halcyon Consortium's terraforming patents depended on the colony's failure being an accident, not a massacre. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: The Smallest Witness
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. A child named Tomas draws the massacre in perfect detail — corridors, numbers, faces — though he cannot speak yet. Ilsa realizes the de-aging preserved what the archive destroyed. Emotional beat: terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Signal From the Core
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A corporate vessel requests docking, claiming to offer rescue. Its manifest lists a 'records integrity officer.' Paloma begins hiding the children and duplicating his logs. Emotional beat: hunted-animal alertness.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The visitors arrive with warrants and a machine designed to overwrite station archives. Paloma stalls them with bureaucratic theater while copying everything to analog tape. Emotional beat: defiance disguised as compliance.

chapters.title: What We Were Before
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Around a station mess-hall table, the aged-back colonists pool their fragmentary memories, reconstructing the night of the fire. Emotional beat: communal mourning becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Officer's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Records officer Dane Voss is genuinely decent — and genuinely committed to the erasure. Their conversations become a duel over whether truth or stability matters more. Emotional beat: uncomfortable sympathy for the enemy.

chapters.title: Tomas Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Tomas finally speaks, naming the officer who gave the order — a name now sitting on the Core's ruling council. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. One survivor, terrified for the children, contacts Voss. The hidden tapes' location is compromised; two are seized and wiped. Emotional beat: heartbreak and the cost of mercy.

chapters.title: Countdown on Vesper-9
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Voss receives orders: sterilize the station, take the children for 'study.' A fleet is eleven hours out. Paloma commits fully to resistance. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Station Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Paloma and Ilsa. They turn the relay station itself into a weapon — rerouting its ancient antenna array, booby-trapping the archive vault, teaching the children the escape routes. Emotional beat: fragile solidarity.

chapters.title: Voss's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Alone with the seized tapes, he hears a child's voice describing his own signature on the order. His certainty cracks. Emotional beat: complicity confronting conscience.

chapters.title: Fire Again
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The corporate team storms the station; the greenhouse burns exactly as the colony did. Ilsa relives her death protecting the children through the smoke. Emotional beat: history repeating, and this time fought.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Climax. Paloma reaches the antenna core under fire and begins transmitting the full unaltered record — logs, drawings, testimony — on every frequency, knowing the fleet will jam it and kill him. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: The Signal Survives
chapters.summary: POV Voss. The broadcast hits open receivers across three systems before the jam closes. Voss, holding the door instead of closing it, lets the last data packet through. Emotional beat: redemption too late to be clean.

chapters.title: Heirs
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The children escape on the Meridian, guided by Ilsa's recovered memories of the helm. Behind them, Vesper-9 goes dark. Ahead, a hundred ships heard the truth. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: When the Colony Falls Again
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa, epilogue. On a new world, the colonists plant gardens and play Paloma's final log each year. Memory is now their institution, not their wound. Final beat: what is remembered cannot be massacred twice.
